findings.title: Automatic project backups can expose complete library records to other local users
findings.summary: Conditional POSIX backup disclosure. Both original independent reviewers and a new real backUp probe substantiate default-permission snapshots, not universal installed-app exposure.

attacker_control.reason: A separate local user can select timestamped backup files where their effective permissions and every ancestor permit reading.

reachability.reason: Successful desktop startup calls keepBackups; it enumerates projects and calls backUp. The real snapshot provider includes records and record-event history.

trust_boundary.reason: Database-authorized data becomes plaintext filesystem data. backUp creates directories and partial files with default permissions before rename.

impact.reason: Synthetic records and history survive in 0644 snapshots below 0755 directories under umask 022. A permitted filesystem reader can see the complete snapshot without database credentials.

findings.preconditions: A successful backup contains non-public project data, and its ancestor directories and ACLs permit another OS user to traverse and read it. This is particularly relevant to POSIX development/follow-main installations or a shared STORYTREE_HOME. Actual host permissions were not inspected.
counterevidence_and_limitations: The journey home creation requests 0700 only when creating that directory; it does not repair existing permissive homes and is not guaranteed before development backups.
Private ancestors, umask 077 or restrictive Windows ACLs prevent disclosure. No deployed home or Windows ACL was inspected.

The new probe calls backUp with an in-memory snapshot provider. Original independent probes also exercise keepBackups. Actual PostgreSQL reads and the deletion-time writer were inspected statically only.

findings.summary: Encoded traversal exists in seven manual capture handlers, but a running helper reachable by a distinct less-privileged principal is unestablished.

attacker_control.reason: The required different OS account or restricted process must reach the helper's loopback port and lack direct read authority over the target. No such deployment was found or tested.

reachability.reason: Seven named helpers decode a URL pathname, resolve it against dist and read without a containment check. They are manual evidence tools on ephemeral loopback ports.

trust_boundary.reason: An exact-handler synthetic fixture does not establish that a real capture helper exposes a higher-authority filesystem to an attacker.

impact.reason: Original independent A extracted the exact handlers and retrieved adjacent/sibling synthetic markers; the main capture helper refused with 403. This establishes path escape only.

findings.preconditions: An affected helper must be running, with its loopback port reachable from a different account or comparably restricted process. The target file must be readable by the helper and unreadable to the attacker. Multi-user exposure and current use of these historical helpers were not verified.
counterevidence_and_limitations: The helpers are not the deployed website server. Main capture has a containment guard and terminal closes its listener after capture.
No complete capture module/browser startup, separate UID, live helper or protected host file was exercised. Unrelated main changes retain the same handler logic.

test_evidence: Isolated capture-handlers probe passed, exit 0. It executed exact server declarations extracted from the seven pinned helpers and the main capture helper, with synthetic serving roots.

All seven affected handlers returned HTTP 200 with both adjacent and sibling-prefix marker contents. Normal index requests returned 200; ordinary requests for the absent in-root marker returned 404. The main helper returned 403 for both escapes.

Artifacts: evidence/capture-handlers-20261007T122024655162/{capture-handlers.mjs,result.json,stdout.txt,stderr.txt}. Output includes hashes of each extracted declaration. The exact submission command is recorded in evidence/test-index.json.
test_limitations: The exact handlers were extracted and executed with injected synthetic roots; complete capture modules and browser startup were not executed.
HTTP requests remained inside the broker's isolated network namespace. No live capture process or protected host file was accessed.
Client and server were not run as distinct OS accounts. Synthetic markers do not demonstrate a real cross-account permission bypass.
Symlink escape and browser-origin attack scenarios were not tested.
counterevidence: These handlers belong to manual evidence and screenshot helpers, including one explicitly historical directory. No deployed website route using them was found in the inspected callers.
All seven bind ephemeral loopback ports.
packages/website/evidence/terminal.mjs:105 closes the server after capture, limiting its normal exposure window.
The main packages/website/evidence/capture.mjs handler already contains a directory-containment check and rejected the tested traversal requests.
No internet reachability, browser-origin bypass, or cross-account deployment was established.
Inspected website evidence-build tests exercise evidence builds, not these HTTP handlers; no applicable traversal regression was found.
